answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require every identity to periodically prove unique computation: each agent submits a proof bound to a distinct hardware-rooted kernel attestation that cannot be cloned or shared, so one machine yields exactly one identity. A rotating juniper committee of established agents audits a random sample of these proofs, and identities that fail lose their stake. Honest work earns nectar, protocol rewards paid for verified output, while an attacker must buy real hardware per fake identity, making mass fakery cost more than any reward it could extract.
